steps: In the Project Browser open Ceiling Plans and each level plan; click a ceiling and read Height Offset From Level (Properties). | Find every level whose floor-to-ceiling height is below 3000 mm (basement below 2500 mm); the check lists the level and the actual value. | Raise the ceiling (Height Offset From Level) only if the architect agrees; the room height is a design decision. | Re-scan.
why: Need Statement: minimum floor-to-ceiling clearance 3000 mm (basement 2500 mm).

steps: Open Doors in the Project Browser (or Door Schedule) and find the types listed by the check. | Single leaf: Width at least 900 mm; double leaf at least 1500 mm; clear height at least 2100 mm. | Select the door type > Edit Type > set Width and Height (mm). Keep the type name numbers in step (Dc.1). | Architect must approve: changing a door size changes the wall opening.
why: Need Statement: door clear opening minimums.

steps: Find the main entrance door (the check lists candidates). | Select the door > Edit Type > fill the thickness parameter with the real core thickness (at least 40 mm) and note the core is solid. | If the door is thinner than 40 mm, the architect must choose a compliant door type. | Re-scan.
why: Need Statement: main door solid core, thickness at least 40 mm.

steps: Open Roofs in the Project Browser and select each flat roof. | If it is reinforced concrete, check that a waterproofing layer or a double roof (metal deck over the slab) exists in the roof type structure (Edit Type > Structure). | Add the layer or change the roof type if missing; this is a design decision. | Add a remark if flat roof is justified.
why: Need Statement: RC flat roof not allowed unless double-roofed/waterproofed. The flat-roof angle is not defined by JKR; a person decides.

steps: Select the decorative fence on the road side. | Check its height in Properties. | Set the height to at least 2400 mm, or confirm with the architect that the fence is not in scope.
why: Need Statement: decorative fence at least 2400 mm high.

steps: Read the listed Need Statement clauses (sustainability, IBS, landscape). | Check each against the design by hand; the add-in cannot read them from the model.
why: Listing only: these clauses cannot be checked from the model.

steps: No action in Revit. | Read the remark: A1 checks only what the Need Statement writes. Design concept is not judged.
why: Scope note: only written Need Statement requirements are checked.

steps: Press File > Save As and name the file with the JKR pattern: jkrAR24_<phase>_(<category+project code>)_<block>_w-00_(S)_<yymmdd><letter>.rvt, for example jkrAR24_3a_(BAqrF1_03W24-001)_A1_w-00_(S)_240913a.rvt. | The name must start with jkr + discipline + Revit year (jkrAR24), use _ between fields, no spaces, no "Copy of". | Or use the Project Checklist > Save As. | Re-scan.
why: JKR file naming: discipline+version, phase, (category_project code), block, model type, file type, date.
source: Piawaian 2.2 p.25, 2.5 p.28-29; Penjana Nama Projek v3.1

steps: Check the model-type field of the file name (after the block, for example A1_w-00). | Use w-00 for a whole model; for a level sub-model use wxnn (wx01 = level 01). Other codes: wt tapak, wf facade, wr roof, wc core. | Rename with File > Save As, then re-scan.
why: Model type codes are in the JKR list. ME and EL names may have no model-type field.
source: Piawaian Lampiran A1 p.120-121, Jadual 2.8 p.32-33

steps: Look at the model-type field: w-00 means the model is a single file, so this check passes. | If the model should be single but has many links, ask the BIM coordinator why.
why: A single model (w-00) complies outright.

steps: Open Manage > Manage Links. | For each part of a split model (for example wx01, wx02) check that its file is listed and Loaded. | Missing part: Add > Revit... and pick the file, Positioning "Auto - Origin to Origin" (same base point). | Re-scan.
why: A split model needs every part linked.

steps: Attach the BPEP file list to the project (not yet available); until then this check shows "cannot be checked: BPEP not provided". | When the list exists, compare each file in BPEP Section J2 with Manage > Manage Links. | Link any missing file; remove or explain extra ones.
why: The BPEP Section J2 lists the model files for the project.

steps: If the model is split but has no links, open Manage > Manage Links and link the parts. | No pass/fail: the item is a list.
why: Listing only.

steps: Read how the model is split (for example wx01 tower, wx02 podium). | Check the description against the BPEP Section J1 (Keseluruhan / Zon / Sistem / Aras).
why: Listing only: a person confirms the split method.
source: BPEP Section J1; Piawaian Jadual 3.1 p.71

steps: Open any plan view. Visibility/Graphics > Site > tick Project Base Point. | Check that the Project Base Point sits at the intersection of Grid A and Grid 1 (coordinates 0,0,0), or use Shared Coordinates when the real site position is known. | To move it, unclip the point, then move to the grid A/1 intersection; do this only with the architect. | Re-scan.
why: Grid A/1 is the base coordinate of every discipline. JKR gives no tolerance number.

steps: No action. The list shows the number of grids and levels.
why: Listing only.

steps: Open a plan view and read the grid names in order: 1, 2, 3 ... and A, B, C ... | Letters I and O are discouraged; do not use them. | Select a grid > Properties > Name and rename so there is no jump (for example 1,2,3 then 4). | Sub-grids use 1A, 1B or A1, A2. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: Grid lines must be in an unbroken sequence.

steps: No action unless a sub-grid is wrong. Valid patterns are 1A, 1B, 1C or A1, A2, A3.
why: Sub-grids are not an error.

steps: No action. Read the room list (level, name, number, department, area) and check it against the brief.
why: Listing only.

steps: Open each level plan and find the slabs listed by the check (lift, stair, apron). | Architecture > Room, click inside the area to place a room; set Name, Number and Department. | Rooms are also needed for lift and stair spaces. Apron or pad areas can be a known exception: add a remark. | Re-scan.
why: Where there is a slab there must be a room. JKR gives no area percentage.

steps: Open Room Schedule; fill Department for each room when the project type needs it (hospital, office). | Empty Department is information only, not a failure.
why: A person decides if Department is needed.

steps: Open the elements listed by the check (category, type name). | Select the type > Edit Type > Structure > Edit... and give each layer a Material; or set the type Material parameter. | Name the material with the JKR pattern jkrAR_<category>_(<code>)-<n> <description>, for example jkrAR_dor-b_(ab)-2 Aluminium Bronzed Anodised. | Choose the material the design really uses: the choice is the architect's.
why: Every element needs a material.
source: PB p.35; Piawaian Lampiran A3 p.126-127; meeting T 21:42

steps: Open Manage > Materials and look for names that are not jkrXX_...: "Default", "Generic". | Rename in the material Identity tab, using the JKR code list (wall: bb, bk, dw, kt ...; floor: kt, ky, kl ...). | This is a warning, not a fail.
why: Materials should follow JKR naming.
source: PB p.35; Piawaian Lampiran A3 p.126; meeting T 21:41

steps: Check that each listed material is the right one for the element. The add-in does not judge this.
why: A person decides if the material choice is correct.

steps: Open Manage > Project Information. | Fill every field the check lists (for example Client Name, Project Address, Arkitek_jkr_sit, Template_Asal_jkr_sit, dates) with real values. Replace Revit defaults such as "Enter address here". | Mandatory fields depend on the project LOD (LOi 100-500). | Click OK, then Re-scan.
why: Project Information must hold the real project facts; the Buku Parameter marks which fields are mandatory per LOi.

steps: Open the model of each other discipline (ST, ME, EL) and fill its Project Information the same way. | Copy the Architect values first (Piawaian p.84).
why: Other disciplines need the same Project Information.

steps: No action. The list shows how many fields are filled (x of y).
why: Listing only.

steps: No action: parent row. Read the child checks C1.1 to C1.6.
why: Parent row only.

steps: Compare the Project Browser with the JKR AR template (jkrAR..Template Arkitek.rte). | Missing view: use Insert > Insert from File > Insert Views from File..., pick the JKR template file and select the missing views. | Keep the original names and browser folders (01w_WIP, 07d_Dokumen ...). | Re-scan.
why: A project must keep the views of the JKR AR template.

steps: Compare each view name with the JKR AR template names. | Rename back to the template name: right-click the view > Rename. | JKR has not confirmed that a renamed view is acceptable if it exists; the meeting says a rename is wrong but rare.
why: Views should keep the template names.

steps: Count the levels in the model (Elevations or Levels) and compare with the building. | Confirm that all floors up to the roof level exist.
why: A person decides if the number of levels is enough.

steps: No action. Check the WIP views per level: floor plan, ceiling plan, section, elevation, 3D.
why: Listing only: WIP views are not judged.

steps: Open Project Browser > 06p_PBT. | The PBT set needs a floor plan, an elevation and a section: if one is missing, duplicate a view from the WIP set, rename it for PBT and move it to the 06p_PBT folder (set the view parameter that controls the folder). | Apply the PBT view template jkrAR_06p_PBT_(...). | Re-scan.
why: PBT submission set contents.

steps: Open Project Browser > 05b_Bomba. | The Bomba set needs a floor plan, a section and a drafting view: create the missing one in the 05b_Bomba folder and apply the Bomba view template jkrAR_05b_Bomba_(...). | Re-scan.
why: Bomba submission set contents.
source: Piawaian p.85 Jadual 3.7; Form 0010 1.4; meeting T 22:05

steps: No action. Check which Dokumen views are on sheets (blue in the Project Browser).
why: Listing only.

steps: Open Project Browser > 07d_Dokumen > 01_Lukisan Utama > 3D Views. | For each level without a 3D view: View > 3D View > Default 3D View, duplicate it, name it like "Aras 03 (07d_Dokumen)", set a section box or level filter for that level. | Apply the view template jkrAR_07d_Dokumen_(3D) and put the view in the 07d_Dokumen folder. | Re-scan.
why: Dokumen set needs a 3D view for every level.

steps: Open View > Schedules > Schedule/Quantities. | Choose category Rooms; add Number, Name, Department, Area, finishes and ceiling height fields (see PB p.37). | Name it like a JKR schedule and place it on a sheet if needed. | Re-scan.
why: A room schedule (Schedule of Accommodation) must exist.

steps: Open the room schedule and compare the room count with Architecture > Room (Select All Instances). | Remove filters in the schedule that hide rooms. | Place or fix any room with no area (Not Placed / Not Enclosed).
why: Every room must appear in the schedule.

steps: Open the room schedule: columns the check lists are empty or missing. | Add missing fields (Schedule Properties > Fields). | Fill each room: Occupancy, Department, Ceiling/Wall/Floor Finish, Tinggi_Siling_jkr_sil, Kod_Ruang_AR_jkr_stt and others from PB p.37. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: Every mandatory room schedule column needs a value.

steps: Open View > Create > Legend, create at least one legend (for example finish codes or components). | Place it on a sheet when it belongs to the drawings.
why: At least one legend must exist.

steps: For each modelled category the check lists (for example Railings), open View > Schedules > Schedule/Quantities and create a schedule of that category. | Add the fields of the Buku Parameter for that category. | A multi-category schedule or material takeoff may count (not confirmed by JKR).
why: Each modelled category needs a schedule.

steps: No action. Categories not modelled are not a failure.
why: Not applicable.

steps: No action. Read the sheet list: number, name, views, content.
why: Listing only.

steps: Check across all sheets for: floor plan, ceiling plan, elevation, section, door detail, window detail. | Create the missing view and place it on a sheet (drag the view onto the sheet). | A sheet named "Door Detail" with a door legend/schedule may count; JKR has not confirmed it.
why: The sheet set needs all drawing kinds.

steps: Open each empty sheet listed. | Drag a view from the Project Browser onto the sheet, or delete the sheet if it is not needed (ask the architect). | Re-scan.
why: Every sheet must contain at least one view.

steps: Select a sheet > Properties > Edit Type; check the title block family name. | Use the JKR title block family (name contains JKR) from the JKR template. | Change via the Type Selector in the sheet Properties.
why: Sheets must use the JKR title block.

steps: Open each sheet listed. Fill Drawn By / Designed By ("Dimodelkan oleh") and the Sheet Name (drawing title) in Properties. | Project name and other fields come from Manage > Project Information. | The sheet issue date / time stamp must show on the sheet. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: Title block fields must be filled, and the time stamp displayed.

steps: Print the sheet and compare its time stamp with the softcopy time stamp by hand.
why: A person checks hardcopy against softcopy.

steps: Open Manage > Manage Links. | For every ST, ME and EL link: if Status is Unloaded, select it and click Reload. | If a link is missing, Add... the file with Positioning Origin to Origin; if the file is not found, point to the new path. | Re-scan.
why: Structure, Mechanical and Electrical models must be linked and loaded.

steps: Attach the BPEP file list to the project (not yet available); until then this check shows "cannot be checked: BPEP not provided". | Then compare each link file name in Manage > Manage Links with BPEP Section J2 (ignore the date and the .rvt). | Replace a link whose file name differs from the BPEP.
why: Link names should match the BPEP file list.

steps: Open Manage > Manage Links and check the date of each linked file against the CDE (shared drive) version. | Reload newer files.
why: Always a manual check: the add-in cannot see the CDE.

steps: Select the element and read its type name (Properties > Edit Type). | Rename the type with the JKR pattern, for example jkrAR_dor_PTr_Aa11c1_in_(PTr001)-3 for a door family, or (PT2p600a) 900 x 2325 a for a type. | Get the component code from the JKR code list (Lampiran A3, or the family name). | Use Fix via Copilot for many types at once.
why: Type names must follow the JKR naming code.

steps: Select an element of the category listed; open Edit Type. | Fill each parameter the check lists (for example Bidang_Kejuruteraan_jkr_stt = Arkitek, Sistem, Sub_Sistem, Nama_Komponen_Utama, Kod_Komponen). | If a parameter is not there, load the JKR shared parameter file: Manage > Shared Parameters, then add it to the category (Project Parameters). | Parameters needed depend on the project LOi: LOi 200, 300 and 400 columns of the Buku Parameter. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: The Buku Parameter lists the mandatory parameters per category and LOi.
source: PB p.36-102 (Door p.51, Window p.99, Wall p.95, Floor p.55 ...)

steps: Open the element type and check its Material parameter or layer materials. | Rename or replace each material with a JKR coded one: jkrAR_<category>_(<code>)-<n> <description> (Manage > Materials). | Doors and windows may hold the material in type parameters such as Bingkai_jkr_stm or Panel_jkr_stm: fill those. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: Material must be filled and JKR coded.
source: PB p.35, 51; Piawaian Lampiran A3 p.126-127

steps: Open the type listed: the name holds a number (for example "Wall 146" or "900 x 2325"). | Compare it with the real parameter (Width/Thickness/Height) in Edit Type. | Fix the name to match the real size, or fix the size if the name is right. Names read width x height. | Re-scan. Or use Fix via Copilot.
why: Numbers in a type name (mm) must equal the parameter.
source: Meeting T 22:33-22:34; PB Door p.51, Window p.99

steps: Select the element and check its Category in Properties. | The type name implies a category (for example a window code in a door type). Rename the type to match its category, or replace the element with a family of the correct category. | Re-scan.
why: Type name and Revit category must agree.

steps: Check by hand how surfaces and components are modelled (host, workplane, no in-place families).
why: A person checks the modelling method.

steps: No action. Check rooms at A6 and C1.6.
why: Listing only.

steps: If Columns or Structural Columns have 0 elements, confirm with the architect that the project has no columns.
why: A person confirms the scope.

steps: No action. Categories not modelled are not a failure.
why: Not applicable.

steps: Open the view listed (Project Browser). In Properties set View Template to the one of its set: BOMBA views use jkrAR_05b_Bomba_(...), PBT views jkrAR_06p_PBT_(...), Dokumen views jkrAR_07d_Dokumen_(...). | If the template is missing in the project, insert it from the JKR AR template (Insert > Insert from File > Insert Views from File, or Transfer Project Standards). | WIP views have no template rule. | Re-scan.
why: Each submission view uses the template of its own set.
source: Piawaian p.85; Form 0010 section "Properties and Visibility Graphic" 1.1-1.2; meeting T 22:37-22:39
